title: Abu Kir the Dyer and Abu Sir the Barber

keywords: abu kir the dyer and abu sir the barber
full_text:
In Alexandria lived two neighbors: Abu Kir, a cunning, deceitful dyer who cheated his customers, and Abu Sir, an honest, gentle barber who served the poor with patient skill. Both were reduced to poverty and agreed to travel together to foreign lands, sharing their earnings as brothers.

They sailed to an uncharted island capital where the art of dyeing was unknown—the inhabitants wore only uncolored white wool. Abu Kir opened a dyeing shop, colored cloth with brilliant indigo, saffron, and madder, and was showered with gold by the King. Intoxicated by wealth, he abandoned his sick friend Abu Sir in a wretched caravanserai.

When Abu Sir recovered through his own resilience, he discovered that the city possessed no public bathhouses. Using his skills, Abu Sir constructed the first magnificent hammam in the kingdom, with marble basins, scented vapors, and massage halls.

The King and the entire court visited the bathhouse, rewarding Abu Sir with palaces and honors.

Abu Kir, seeing his former partner’s prosperity, was consumed by toxic envy. He crept to the King, whispering that Abu Sir was a foreign spy who intended to poison the royal bath!

The deceived King condemned Abu Sir to be sewn into a sack and cast into the sea.

However, the honest captain of the execution barge, whose sick son Abu Sir had previously healed with soothing remedies, rescued the barber and substituted an empty sack of stones!

While fishing in the bay, Abu Sir’s net caught a fish containing the King’s lost signet ring!

Abu Sir returned the ring to the monarch, the foul conspiracy was exposed, and Abu Kir fell into the very pit of execution he had dug for his innocent friend. The King made Abu Sir his Grand Vizier, proving that honest virtue outlasts the darkest malice.
moral: Treacherous malice and envy will ultimately destroy the schemer, while gentle virtue is vindicated.
